subject: Post-demo: Zymble integration — auth options, rotation, and SDK next steps
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Turner <alicia.turner@zymblehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo: Zymble integration — auth options, rotation, and SDK next steps

Hi Alicia — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can lock down an actionable plan:  

Summary of what we covered
- Demo highlights: real-time classification + reranker pipeline, embeddings store for similarity search, structured output via tool-calling for downstream systems.
- Integration focus: SDK onboarding, authentication patterns (API key vs OAuth2/JWT/service accounts), routing for multi-region failover.

Redwood recommended auth approach (based on Zymble constraints)
- Recommended: service-account JWT (OAuth2 assertion) + short-lived bearer tokens (recommended lifetime: 15m–1h) issued by Zymble’s token broker or Redwood private control-plane if you deploy Private.
- Why: avoids long-lived API keys in code, aligns with SOC2 controls (short-lived creds + KMS-wrapped private keys), supports delegated service accounts for per-team isolation.
- Rotation: rotate signing keys at least quarterly; maintain one active and one staging key for seamless rollovers. Automate rotations via KMS/HSM where possible.

SDK setup / dev experience
- We’ll provide an SDK quickstart that supports both API-key-based dev flow and OAuth2/JWT production flow. Example commands and sample project attached (sdk-quickstart-sample.tar.gz).
- Suggest a two-stage rollout: 1) internal devs use API keys + local caching, 2) production switch to short-lived tokens + service accounts.

Routing / structured output notes
- Route requests by customer priority (low-latency vs low-cost) using per-route policies in the SDK config.
- For tool-calling / structured JSON outputs, enable strict schema validation on Redwood’s response hooks so your backend can safely parse and persist results.

Next steps / asks for Zymble
1) Confirm whether Zymble will host a token broker or prefer Redwood to mint short-lived tokens for you (Private deployment only).
2) Share a contact on the SRE/security side (cc’d here) for the key rotation policy and SOC2 checklist.
3) Pick a 60-minute deep technical call this week for the SRE + Dev leads so Ben can walk through the token handshake and SDK bootstrapping.

Attaching: redwood-integration-patterns.pdf (integration patterns, auth tradeoffs), zymble-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (draft MAP).

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

—
Logan Wright

Thanks Logan — solid recap. A few quick clarifying questions before we schedule the deep technical call:  

1) Delegated service accounts: we need per-environment service accounts (dev/stage/prod) and the ability to scope permissions per service account. Does Redwood support impersonation flows or token exchange so our pipeline can mint tokens scoped to a specific env?
2) Rotation SLA: our compliance team prefers maximum key lifetime = 90 days, with automated rollbacks for failed rotations. Can you confirm automation hooks (webhooks or API) we can call during rollovers?
3) Embeddings store: does your recommended flow keep embeddings encrypted at rest with separate key per-tenant? We also need the option for us to bring our own KMS.

We’re generally aligned to short-lived tokens but want to understand the operational model (who runs the broker, what logs we get for audits). s re-team@zymblehealth.com will own the technical session; I’m copying them here.

Also attached: Zymble_SSO_and_Security_Reqs.pdf (internal checklist).

Best,

Alicia — great questions. Below are concrete answers and implementation notes so your SREs can validate against the SOC2 checklist.

Service account / impersonation model
- Redwood supports two patterns: 1) direct OAuth2 JWT assertion where a service account key signs an assertion and exchanges it for a short-lived token; 2) token-exchange where Zymble’s token broker mints short-lived tokens after authenticating internal users (recommended for strict separation).
- For per-env scoping: create separate service accounts (dev/stage/prod) and attach granular roles to each. Our SDK honors scope claims (aud, exp) and routes tokens to the proper route policies.

Rotation automation
- Key rotation: we provide APIs to upload new public keys and stage them; rotation can be automated via CI to call Redwood’s /keys/stage and /keys/activate endpoints. Webhook on activation is available to notify your orchestration system of completion.
- Recommended schedule: 90-day key lifetime, daily smoke test after activation, automatic revert to previous key on repeated signature failures for 10 minutes.

Bring-your-own-KMS / data encryption
- Embeddings and KV caches are encrypted at rest; we support BYOK via Cloud KMS (GCP/AWS/Azure) or HSM for Private deployments. Separate key per-tenant is supported in Dedicated and Private modes; Hosted supports tenant separation with envelope encryption and a per-tenant KEK.

Audit logs / evidence
- We can stream audit logs (auth grants, token minting, key activations) to your SIEM via secure syslog or to an S3 bucket with lifecycle policies. We also provide signed timestamped records for each token mint.

Sample bootstrap snippet (pseudo):
- Create service account + upload public key to Redwood
- CI: call /keys/stage -> /keys/activate (on success run smoke test)
- App: sign JWT assertion -> POST /oauth2/token (grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer) -> receive short-lived bearer token

I’ve dropped a link to a more detailed runbook here: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-zymble-auth-design (attached into MAP). I can walk through the exact API calls in the technical session.

If Zymble prefers Redwood to host the token broker (Private unreachable), we can operate token minting with strict tenancy and provide the same audit trails; that option adds a contractual requirement around key custody.

Soojin — can you propose 2 slots tomorrow for the 60-minute SRE + dev deep-dive? Prefer 10:00–12:00 PT.
